1.title: Exam Technique and Final Review
1.text: Welcome to Module fifteen: Exam Technique and Final Review. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. The pairs the exam likes to confuse. The lists to know by heart. Technique for each question style. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Scope: All categories. Exam format: forty multiple-choice questions in sixty minutes; twenty-six correct answers (sixty-five percent) pass. Validated against: the official eye til Foundation (Version five) syllabus, version five point zero (February two thousand twenty-six).

1.title: The pairs the exam likes to confuse
1.text: The pairs the exam likes to confuse. Output or outcome. deliverable or result for a stakeholder. Utility or warranty. fit for purpose or fit for use. Sponsor or customer or user. pays or defines needs and owns outcomes or uses. Basic or cooperative or collaborative. transaction or mutual benefit or partnership. Transfer of goods or access to resources. ownership passes or use without owning. Event or incident. change of state or unplanned interruption. Problem or error or known error. cause or fault or understood but unresolved, with workaround.

1.title: The pairs the exam likes to confuse, continued
1.text: The pairs the exam likes to confuse. Continuous delivery or deployment. ready to release or released automatically. Core or enabling value stream. consumer feels it or supports the core. Mapping or management. shows the flow or improves it. C S F (critical success factor) or metric. must be true or how it is measured. gen A I or agentic A I. creates content or acts toward a goal.

1.title: The lists to know by heart
1.text: The lists to know by heart. Eight lifecycle activities. discover, design, acquire, build, transition, operate, deliver, support. Five eye til Value System components. guiding principles, governance, value chain, management practices, continual improvement. Seven guiding principles. focus on value; start where you are; progress iteratively with feedback; collaborate and promote visibility; think and work holistically; keep it simple and practical; optimize and automate. Four dimensions. organizations and people; information and technology; partners and suppliers; value streams and processes.

1.title: The lists to know by heart, continued
1.text: The lists to know by heart. Seven improvement steps. vision, current state, target state, how to get there, action, evaluation, momentum. Six A I capabilities. creation, curation, clarification, cognition, communication, coordination. pestle (political, economic, social, technological, legal and environmental). political, economic, social, technological, legal, environmental.

1.title: Technique for each question style
1.text: Technique for each question style. Standard. Read the last line, name the term, eliminate. Negative. Rewrite as "find the false one"; check each option. Missing word(s). Read the sentence with each option; choose the definition. List. Mark each statement true or false; pick the pair. Old wording alert: if an option says service value system, service value chain, plan, improve, engage, general, service and technical practices, it is eye til four language and is probably a distractor for Version five. Exam tip: Before you answer, ask: is this an eye til four word? Service value system, service value chain, plan, improve, engage and three practice groups are old wording and rarely the right Version five answer.

1.title: Technique for each question style, continued
1.text: Technique for each question style. Exam tip: With no negative marking, answer every question; flag the hard ones and return with the time left.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Which list names the eye til Value System components? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Guiding principles, governance, value chain, management practices, continual improvement. B is the lifecycle, C the dimensions, D the improvement steps.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A user reports that the payment page is down. Which term describes the report? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Incident. An unplanned interruption is an incident.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which statements are C O R R E C T? (one) Utility means fit for purpose. (two) Warranty means fit for purpose. (three) Output is a deliverable and outcome is a result. (four) A sponsor defines requirements for the service. The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: one and three. Utility is fit for purpose, and output is a deliverable while outcome is a result.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Identify the missing word(s). A blank is a problem that has been analyzed but not resolved, usually with a workaround. The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Known error. That is a known error.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Which principle says to improve a process before automating it? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Optimize and automate. Optimize first, then automate.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A team draws the steps, waits and handoffs of its order process to see where work slows. What is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Value stream mapping. Drawing steps and waits is value stream mapping.

1.title: Practice Question 7
1.text: Question seven. Which statement about the lifecycle activities is C O R R E C T? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: They are not sequential or linear and can be used iteratively. The activities loop and can be iterated.

1.title: Practice Question 8
1.text: Question eight. How many marks do you need to pass? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: twenty-six. The pass mark is twenty-six of forty.

1.title: Practice Question 9
1.text: Question nine. Which capability of the eye til A I Capability Model covers natural interaction such as chat and voice? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Communication. Communication is natural interaction.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the pass mark? Answer: twenty-six of forty (sixty-five percent). Question two. Which category has the highest weight? Answer: The eye til Value System, at forty percent. Question three. Name the eight lifecycle activities. Answer: Discover, design, acquire, build, transition, operate, deliver, support.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Name the seven guiding principles. Answer: Focus on value; start where you are; progress iteratively with feedback; collaborate and promote visibility; think and work holistically; keep it simple and practical; optimize and automate. Question five. What is the eye til four name for the eye til Value System? Answer: The service value system. Question six. What is the difference between governance and management? Answer: Governance directs and controls (evaluate, direct, monitor); management runs the day-to-day work.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Exam: forty questions, sixty minutes, twenty-six to pass, no negative marking. Weights: key terms thirty, dimensions ten, lifecycle ten, Value System forty, value streams five, A I two point five, frameworks two point five. Method: keyword, name the term, eliminate, choose the definition. Old wording: service value system, six-activity value chain, three practice groups. Always: answer every question. If this course is helping you, please subscribe to the channel and hit the bell icon, so you get a notification when the next video is out. That completes the course. Good luck with the exam.
